dedupe_keys.name: dzsf potential study of photovoltaic applications on rail infrastructure in germany tuv rheinland research report 57 2024

description: This potential study, commissioned by the German Centre for Rail Transport Research (DZSF) at the Federal Railway Authority and carried out by TÜV Rheinland from November 2021, estimates how much solar power could be generated on and in German rail infrastructure and fed directly into the 16.7 Hz traction power network. Contents: market research on PV systems suited to railways, the effects of vibration and soiling in the track bed, usable areas (about 30 km2 in and around the network of about 33,500 km), installable power and energy, and three scenarios: A, 380 GWh a year from ground-mounted systems, stations, canopies and noise barriers at low cost; B, 910 GWh; and C, 2,940 GWh a year from all technical options at up to 25 ct/kWh, about 27% of the railway's roughly 11,000 GWh annual demand. Coverage: Germany. Format and access: a 260-page report published in 2024 as DZSF research report 57, in German, with an English press release of 23 September 2024. Licence and cost: free to download; no licence stated. Caveats: technical potential, not a site list, and direct feed-in was still being trialled. The scenario figures can set on-site generation potential for rail energy supply in capacity planning and optimisation models. It relates to the European roads and railways vertical PV potential study in the catalogue.
